author: Mark Atwood
text:
Three roughly-equal options presented by the bead, each with real cost. This is a workspace-canonical-conformance vs test-discipline tradeoff that needs a human call:

(i) Drop inline test_support + inline unit tests, move all tests to tests/ using MemoryBackend. PROS: matches canonical mail-server (which has no inline unit tests), single test surface, fewer trait impls to keep in sync (one less full JmapBackend + MetadataBackend impl). CONS: loses fine-grained unit testing for the validate_metadata_filter walker, the validate-and-collect destroy loop, and other pre-delegate handler logic. ~13 inline unit tests would need to be rewritten as integration tests, doubling their bulk. The added unit tests under bd:JMAP-826m.1 (6 tests) and bd:JMAP-826m.34 (7 tests) all use MockBackend.

(ii) Move test_support out of src/lib.rs into tests/common/mod.rs. PROS: stops the 350-line MockBackend from polluting the main crate compilation; keeps unit-test capability. CONS: integration tests cannot easily test crate-private items (the validate_metadata_filter / walk_filter_for_unknown_keys helpers in metadata.rs would need to become pub(crate) which exposes them to dispatch consumers as well). Workaround is to leave thin wrapper tests in src/metadata.rs that just exercise the public handler entry points; the bulky MockBackend itself lives in tests/common/.

(iii) Accept the duplication and document. PROS: no refactoring, current tests stay green, no canonical-divergence beyond what already exists. CONS: every future trait method addition needs to land in two backend impls (Metadata's MockBackend AND MemoryBackend); this has bitten the workspace already (the new principal_id seam, the per-bead.13 unsupported_object_type guard).

Recommendation: option (i). The canonical-template rule and the fact that the existing inline unit tests all exercise call paths that can be exercised via the dispatcher in integration tests means the unit/integration boundary is artificial here. The 350 lines of duplicate MockBackend infrastructure is the real cost and removing it would be net-positive. But this is a significant refactor (touching 13 unit tests across 2 files plus the entire test_support module) that I'd rather not start without human authorization — the 'while I'm here' workspace AGENTS.md rule pushes the other way.
